messages.author: 1080eb2669b76d80
messages.subject: RRO and Intel MKL
parts:
I have been using R and Intel MKL for a while. Now I am surprised by
two things when it comes to install RRO and MKL.

- as RRO is open source licensed, why use Intel MKL, proprietary paid
licenced, to provide Blas ? Why not use open openblas[1] instead?
- your documentation refers to install RRO then install MKL. Why not
install Blas library first, then build RRO with "./configure
--with-blas=" as mentioned in intel article[2] ?

Thank you for hints.


[1]http://www.openblas.net/
[2]https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/build-r-301-with-intel-c-compiler-and-intel-mkl-on-linux

--

google.com/+arnaudgabourygabx

messages.author: 88275a537c4bd7d2
messages.subject: Re: RRO and Intel MKL
parts:
Hi Arnaud,

We use the MKL because in our research it provides the best performance on a wide range of platforms. We're pleased that we're able to partner with Intel to offer it to all RRO users free of charge, as an optional add-on to Revolution R Open.

You're welcome to build RRO (or R) from source using the BLAS library of your choice. Our build instructions at https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/blob/master/README.md are a good starting point. The R Core Group also provide some useful tips for building R with other BLAS libraries at:
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-admin.html#BLAS

Hope this helps,
# David Smith

messages.author: 67f7081cbd450705
messages.subject: Re: RRO and Intel MKL
parts:
There are some other programs that use the Intel MKL too. The other one that comes to my mind is Matlab. The MKL is finely tuned for Intel processors. It works well on other processors too. I use Intel Phi coprocessors and the MKL has an automatic offload option. If I use anything else, I have to rewrite my program to use the Phi's. 

I will admit I am interested in using the AMD ACML with R or RRO. I read that it does an automatic off-load onto GPUs. As someone that has an AMD processor and AMD dual GPU, I'd be interested to benchmark it on my system.

messages.author: 88275a537c4bd7d2
messages.subject: Re: RRO and Intel MKL
parts:
Hi Hamad,

Yes. You can use RRO with MKL for any purpose, including commercial use. 

The MKL is a separate download, which we distribute under agreement with Intel. You do not need a commercial MKL Intel license to use it. You can review the specific licence agreement for its use when you install the MKL component, but it does not preclude commercial use.

Hope this helps,
David Smith
